statement: Lambda's rendered on-demand pricing tables showed no H200, GB200, GB300 or B300 line items on 2026-08-05, so its newest publicly rentable part is B200.
why: Which parts a large GPU cloud will publicly rent by the hour is a read on where the newest accelerators actually sit — absent SKUs suggest that capacity is either not deployed or committed elsewhere rather than sold on demand.

impact.mechanism: Missing newest-generation SKUs on a major renter's public price list indicates limited on-demand availability of those parts, tightening the effective supply of rentable frontier capacity.

evidence.source: Lambda (Lambda Labs) — official GPU Cloud pricing page
evidence.excerpt: no NVIDIA H200, GB200, GB300 or B300 line items appeared in the rendered on-demand pricing tables on this page on 2026-08-05

confidence.basis: The absence is stated plainly in the snapshot, but it rests on secondary-tier open-web evidence from a single publisher (Lambda) and an absence can also reflect page rendering, so confidence is held at medium.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend unknown -> unknown); sources: Lambda (Lambda Labs) — official GPU Cloud pricing page, RunPod — official GPU pricing page
